extracted.intended_audience: taxonomists and systematic zoologists working on freshwater sponges (Spongillidae), museum curators, and biodiversity researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Diagnostic criteria and descriptive standards for distinguishing genera and species of freshwater sponges (Spongillidae), covering spicule and gemmule morphology, skeleton architecture, measurements, distribution, type deposition, and ecological/biological notes used in formal species accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free microscleres morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: The free microscleres consist as a rule of several or many shafts meeting together in several or many planes at a common centre, which is usually nodular; the free ends of these shafts often possess rudimentary rotulæ. Occasionally a free microsclere may be found that is a true monaxon and sometimes such spicules are more or less distinctly birotulate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish genera (e.g., Dosilia) from other genera like Ephydatia; presence/absence, number of shafts, nodular centre, and any rudimentary rotulæ are diagnostic features; note possible exceptions (occasional monaxon forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton architecture (radiating fibres vs reticulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The skeleton consists mainly of radiating fibres which bifurcate frequently in such a way that a bush-like structure is produced. Transverse fibres are very feebly developed and are invisible to the naked eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skeleton structure (radiating, bifurcating, bush-like; feathery appearance) is a genus-level character (e.g., Dosilia). Record degree of reticulation, presence/absence of transverse fibres, and overall appearance (feathery, dense, stony).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule morphology (coat, air-spaces, spicule arrangement, foraminal tubule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules spherical, usually numerous and of rather large size; each covered by a thick layer of minute air-spaces, among which the gemmule-spicules are arranged vertically, often in two or even three concentric series; a single short foraminal tubule; the pneumatic coat confined externally by a delicate membrane, with small funnel-shaped pits over the spicules of the outer series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed structure of the gemmule (shape, number, size, air-space layer, concentric series of spicules, position/shape of foraminal tubule, pneumatic coat features) is strongly diagnostic at species and genus levels; describe coat thickness, presence of funnel-shaped pits, and arrangement of spicules (vertical, concentric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of bubble-cells in the parenchyma
rubrics_metrics.description: Possession of bubble-cells in the parenchyma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish closely related species (e.g., distinguishes E. meyeni from E. fluviatilis); explicitly note presence/absence of bubble-cells in descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton-spicule surface texture (smooth vs spiny/serrated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Skeleton-spicules smooth (or spiny, blunt, strongly spiny); edges of rotulæ smooth instead of serrated in some genera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surface texture of skeleton-spicules (smooth, spiny, blunt, nodular) and edge character of rotulæ (smooth vs serrated) are key diagnostic characters; record degree and distribution of spination and whether disk edges are serrated, undulated, or smooth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative length of gemmule-spicule shafts vs rotule diameter
rubrics_metrics.description: The shaft extending not at all or very little beyond the disks; in other species shafts are relatively long — e.g., the shafts not extending beyond their surface but clearly seen from above as circular umbones; or shafts relatively long compared with rotule diameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and record whether shafts project beyond rotulæ (umbo), their length relative to disk diameter, and whether shafts are long or short — used to distinguish species (e.g., E. meyeni vs E. mülleri).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type specimen and repository
rubrics_metrics.description: TYPE in the British Museum; a fragment in the Indian Museum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always report type material and repository (museum) and any fragments; include type locality and museum accession if possible as standard practice for taxonomic accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical distribution and localities
rubrics_metrics.description: GEOGRAPHICAL DISTRIBUTION.--India and Sumatra. _Localities_:--BENGAL, Calcutta and neighbourhood; MADRAS PRESIDENCY, Cape Comorin, Travancore; BOMBAY PRESIDENCY, Island of Bombay; HIMALAYAS, Bhim Tal, Kumaon (alt. 4,500 feet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List geographic range and specific localities (provinces, towns, altitudes) for each species; note apparent range discontinuities and biogeographic remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecology and substrate preference
rubrics_metrics.description: This species is never found on floating objects but always on stones or brickwork; grows on artificial stonework at the edge of the water; often occupies the same position in succeeding years; may consist of a dead base and living upper layer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include habitat and substrate preferences (floating vs attached to stone/plant/wood), seasonal occurrence, and typical microhabitats; note ecological interactions (e.g., incolæ such as larvae) and growth behavior (layers, persistence across years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotule edge character (smooth vs serrated/undulated/nodulose)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rotulæ of the gemmule-spicules... are homogeneous, have smooth instead of serrated edges; in some species disks are undulated and nodulose rather than serrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record whether rotulæ edges are smooth, serrated, undulated or nodulose — an important generic and specific character; mention any variation or intermediate conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality or inequality of upper and lower rotulæ
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotules of the gemmule-spicules equal or nearly so; or the upper rotule of the gemmule-spicules distinctly smaller than the lower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether rotulæ are equal, nearly equal, or upper distinctly smaller than lower — used in keys to separate species (e.g., Trochospongilla key).

rubrics_metrics.name: Birotulate condition of gemmule-spicules
rubrics_metrics.description: All those species in which all the gemmule-spicules are definitely birotulate and have smooth edges to their disks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of birotulate gemmule-spicules (both disks present) is a genus-level diagnostic; note exceptions and any spicules with reduced upper rotula (as in Tubella).

rubrics_metrics.name: Position and abundance of gemmules within sponge
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules very numerous and scattered throughout the sponge; or gemmules numerous, situated at the base of the sponge in irregular, one-layered patches; or gemmules sometimes absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe gemmule distribution (throughout, at base, in patches), abundance (numerous, few, absent), and their typical placement (in cages, on surface, embedded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative measurements and average measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Average measurements: Diameter of gemmule 0.2 × 0.18 mm; Length of skeleton-spicule 0.28"; Length of birotulate-spicule 0.175"; Diameter of rotula 0.02"; and species-specific measurement tables comparing specimens from different regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measurements (lengths, diameters) for spicules, gemmules, rotulæ, and give averages and ranges; compare material from different localities when possible; explicit numeric data are essential for species delimitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule pneumatic coat characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules clothed when mature with a thin microcell coat in which the birotulates are arranged with overlapping rotulæ, their outer rotulæ level with the surface; or clothed with a thick granular pneumatic coat with relatively large but irregular air-spaces among which the spicules stand with the rotulæ overlapping alternately, a funnel-shaped pit in the coat descending from the surface to the upper rotula of each of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe coat thickness, cell structure (microcell), air-space size/distribution, arrangement of gemmule-spicules within the coat, and presence of pits or projections; these features are diagnostic and variable by species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule aperture (foraminal aperture) shape and position
rubrics_metrics.description: A single aperture depressed; foraminal aperture circular, situated on an eminence; single aperture situated on an eminence on the apex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record shape (depressed, on eminence, tubular), position (apex, on eminence), and number (single) of the gemmule aperture (foraminal tubule) as part of the gemmule description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flesh-spicule presence and morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Flesh-spicules occasionally amphioxous or birotulate and with a single shaft, more frequently consisting of many shafts meeting in a distinct central nodule; flesh-spicules with distinct rotules, the recurved spines numbering 4 to 6; shafts irregularly spiny, usually more or less nodular at the tip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note presence/absence, form (amphioxous, birotulate, multi-shafted), ornamentation (recurved spines, nodules), relative size, and arrangement; flesh-spicule morphology helps separate species and varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline for creating new genus based on gemmule/spicule characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Species with free microscleres similar to those of these forms but with heterogeneous or tubelliform gemmule-spicules will probably need the creation of a new genus or new genera for their reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Erect new genera when combinations of characters (e.g., free microscleres type together with markedly different gemmule-spicule structure) cannot be accommodated within existing genera; explicitly justify generic changes by contrasting key characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule layering and relative spicule sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmule with two layers of gemmule-spicules; those of the inner layer not markedly smaller than those of the outer; or gemmule with two layers of gemmule-spicules, the outer of which contains spicules of much greater size than the inner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report number of gemmule layers and relative sizes of spicules in each layer; used in keys (e.g., Corvospongilla) to separate species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence or absence of rotulæ on gemmule-spicules (genus-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spongillidæ in which the gemmule-spicules are without a trace of rotulæ and the flesh-spicules have slender cylindrical shafts that bear at or near either end a circle of strong recurved spines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of rotulæ on gemmule-spicules is a defining genus-level trait (e.g., Corvospongilla); record accompanying characters such as flesh-spicule ornamentation and overall skeleton strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall skeleton strength and texture (hard/stony vs delicate/coarse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Skeleton often dense, forming a close reticulation; in some species the skeleton is so compact and rigid that the sponge may be described as stony; in others the skeleton is delicate with branches diverging widely, containing a considerable amount of chitin, rendering it resistant in spite of delicacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe skeleton firmness (hard, brittle, friable, stony, delicate), presence of chitin, degree of interlocking of spicules, and relation to habit (sheet, cushion, masses); skeleton strength supports ecological and taxonomic interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spicule ornamentation details (recurved spines, conical spines, nodular tips)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spines: rotulæ often bear a distinct circle of recurved spines; shafts armed with a few stout conical spines standing out at right angles; spicules irregularly spiny, usually more or less nodular at the tip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record type, number, distribution and form of spines (recurved, conical), presence of nodules, and whether edges of rotulæ bear spines; such micro-ornamentation is routinely illustrated and measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule adherence and grouping (single, paired, enclosed in cages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules strongly adherent, arranged in small groups, either single or double; each gemmule enclosed more or less distinctly by a circle or several circles of flesh-spicules; each gemmule enclosed in an open, irregular cage of skeleton-spicules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether gemmules are adherent or free, occur singly or in pairs, and whether they are enclosed in cages of spicules; these features affect dispersal and are diagnostic.
